ety.text: Arabic قَهْوَة (qahwa)bor. Ottoman Turkish قهوه (kahve)bor. Italian caffèbor. Dutch koffiebor. English coffee Borrowed from Dutch koffie, from Italian caffè, from Ottoman Turkish قهوه (kahve), from Arabic قَهْوَة (qahwa). Doublet of café and caffè and cognate with the words for "coffee" in other major European languages, most of which are derived from the Turkish and Italian words.

senses.d: A beverage made by infusing the beans of the coffee plant in hot water.
ex: He and his friends used to order coffee whenever they went out.

senses.d: A serving of this beverage.
The seeds of the plant used to make coffee, called ‘beans’ due to their shape.
The powder made by roasting and grinding the seeds.
A tropical plant of the genus Coffea.
A pale brown color, like that of milky coffee.
The end of a meal, when coffee is served.
ex: He did not stay for coffee.

senses.d: Of a pale brown colour, like that of milk coffee.
Of a table: a small, low table suitable for people in lounge seating to put coffee cups on.
To drink coffee.
ex: I rushed into my cabin, coffeed, wined, and went to bed sobbing.
We had coffee’d with the scoundrel[…]

senses.d: To give coffee to.
ex: There we were met by enterprising citizens and coffeed and sandwiched by pretty girls.
Five soldiers had been sandwiched and coffeed at the Elks canteen, were a little short of money, needed haircuts.

senses.d: A closed box in which the body of a dead person is placed for burial.
ex: Plans to carry the Queen's coffin from Edinburgh to London by rail were scrapped in favour of travel in a Royal Air Force cargo aircraft.

ex: Of the paste a coffin I will rear.

senses.d: A conical paper bag, used by grocers.
ex: The smoke of this Hearbe, which they receaue at the mouth through certaine coffins, suche as the Grocers do vse to put in their Spices.
